method: morphological description of adult female and male specimens from a plankton tow
conditions: Type series from one oblique tow (0-935 m, ORI net, 330 um mesh) in the Kuroshio region, Japan, on 28 November 2018, fixed in formalin seawater: holotype undissected adult female NSMT-Cr 31562, allotype adult male NSMT-Cr 31563, paratypes one dissected and one undissected female; the eye structure is described for the adult female (Description heading and Diagnosis), and the male description does not mention the eyes; no variation among specimens is reported

source.authors: Komeda S, Ohtsuka S, Huys R
source.title: A new genus and species of oceanic planktonic Tisbidae (Crustacea, Copepoda, Harpacticoida) with enlarged modified eyes

quote: The most distinguishable feature of G. guttatum gen. et sp. nov. is the presence of large, paired, frontal modified eyes, each consisting of a baculiform ocellus, a globular (Gicklhorn’s?) organ, and a semi-parabolic plate.
note: Abstract sentence; the Diagnosis says 'Cephalic region with large, paired, modified eyes' and the female Description gives 'a middorsal pair of baculiform ocelli' with one pair of globular organs, each surrounded by a thin semi-parabolic plate. The authors suggest only that the eyes may help detect bioluminescent food particles; that is a hypothesis in the paper and is not filed here. Family and order as printed in the Taxonomy section (Order Harpacticoida Sars, 1903; Family Tisbidae Stebbing, 1910); the species was described in this paper and no checklist was opened (WoRMS is refused by desk rule).
